items.name: Jurassic Wild - Episode 1 | Journey for Survival
items.description:
"Journey for Survival" is the first episode of Jurassic Wild.
It tells the story of a Yutyrannus fighting to survive in a harsh, cold environment.
I hope you’ll enjoy it :D I created this episode using Jurassic World Evolution 3, with incredible narration by Kat Mackay.

items.name: Pre-History: Outliers | Episode 1 | A Carnotaurus paleo animation
items.description: Every individual living life form are unique, and sometimes they are born with genetic mutations. And dinosaurs, the living and breathing animals they were, are no exception. The animals that are born different can be referred to as "Outliers". In this episode of Pre-History, we explore a very curious case of a female Albino Carnotaurus. Her skin itself was rare as it is, for her to survive till adulthood as well, was nothing short of a miracle.

items.name: "Hunted by Moonlight" | Dinosauria Series
items.description: "Hunted by Moonlight" is a bit different from the rest of the Dinosauria Series. It's a scary story inspired by old gothic fairy tales. I'm particularly fond of the "fairy tale horror" subgenre, but I've never seen it combined with dinosaurs or paleo-media before. I'm overall very proud of the result, and I hope you all enjoy it too! :D"

items.name: Forgotten Bloodlines: Agate | Official Opening Scene
items.description: "Forgotten Bloodlines: Agate" will be a photorealistic animated documentary focusing on prehistoric creatures 20 million years ago, narrated by the wonderful Nigel Marven. It takes place in the early Miocene of the Agate Fossil Beds, one of the richest collections of fossil creatures from the era, including strange horse-like animals with claws, carnivorous hippo ancestors, and rhinos the size of a dog. Over the course of three 15 minute episodes, you will be taken back to a place forgotten to time.
items.creditsLine: Created and directed by Max "Amber" Bellomio.

items.name: THE HATCHLING | Original Dinosaur Short Film
items.description: Introducing ‘THE HATCHLING,’’ an original short film that transports you to a world where dinosaurs and man coexist. Nestled within the picturesque outskirts of Pine Ridge, a tight-knit group is thrust into a thrilling adventure to help reunite a baby Deinocheirus with its family in the sun-soaked wilds. Alongside evading the wrath of prehistoric beasts, our heroes are entangled in a web of forces who wish to capture the infant for their dubious agendas.

items.name: Triceratops | Lunch Time
items.description: "Every animal we have studied turns out smarter than we initially thought. In this video I want to show a speculative social dynamic in a herd of Triceratops, where more senior and larger individuals are respected. They also have strict rules and time-based behaviors that would not be tolerated if broken. Inspired by elephants herds, this animation aim to show the Triceratosp as a fascinating and socially complex animal.Want to learn how to animate with Blender? "
items.freeTags: North America, Late Cretaceous, Tyrannosaurus rex, T.rex, Triceratops

items.name: Tyrannosaurus rex | Bone Bed
items.description: "The courtship behavior of modern birds are extremely diverse and unique. One bird in particular called the Bowerbird would build structures out of branches and decorate them with colorful objects to attract mates. This extraordinary behavior is what inspired me to make this 3D animation, with the male T.rex gathering skulls and bones of prey animals and lay them out in a mass display, making essentially a Bone Bed, to try and impress it's partner that it is a capable hunter. While also performing a "dance" that highlights it's strength and battle scars, hoping to be accepted and carry on the bloodline of one of the greatest predator in Earth's history."
items.freeTags: North America, Late Cretaceous, Tyrannosaurus rex, T.rex, Triceratops

items.name: Spinosaurus | The Gathering
items.description: "Having the idea from seeing large quantities of crocodiles gathering for sunbathing, I thought to myself perhaps Spinosaurus could have exhibited similar behaviors. They are often depicted as solitary animal in paleo media, but the sheer size difference in adult and juvenile suggests to me Spinosaurus may have been very vulnerable to other large carnivores, which the Kem Kem formation had no shortage of, through out its life span and only become near untouchable once it is fully grown. Therefor Spinosaurus of various age and sizes may have gather in large groups, seeking safety from their numbers and the largest individuals in the herd. This video is my attempt at recreating this idea in #blender , using my latest #spinosaurus model."

items.name: Tyrannosaurus rex | Lazy Morning
items.description: "It's been a long time coming, but I finally got up my butt to make another animation. And what else but with a brand new T.rex model to showcase. It was a T.rex that was the first 3D model I ever tried to make seriously, and snowballed me down this path of being a 3D artist for a living. Hopefully this new and improved 2025 version shows I've somewhat improved in my craft, though there are still much I felt like I could have done better."
items.freeTags: North America, Late Cretaceous, Tyrannosaurus Rex, T.rex

items.name: Diplocaulus are prowling
items.description: Imagine this: 270 million years ago, you step into a Permian forest. No humans of course — and no mammals either. You find yourself in a radically different world, where some regions were dry and harsh, but pockets of lush, swampy environments still existed. Swamps like this, though less common than in the previous period, Carboniferous, did exist — and here you can see a Diplocaulus, a boomerang-headed amphibian resting in the shade.

items.name: T.rex drinking in the valley
items.description: Imagine this: 66 million years ago, a Tyrannosaurus rex stands by a river. The air is heavy, warm, and filled with distant calls. He lifts his head — alert. His forward-facing eyes help him track movement and judge distance with very good precision. This scene was created from a real river in southern France (Hérault), transformed into a Cretaceous setting through photobashing and natural lighting.

items.name: Riojavenatrix lacustris
items.description:
Riojavenatrix lacustris is a newly described spinosaurid, published on February 19, 2024. Initially thought to belong to Baryonyx, the fossils revealed a unique combination of features that led to the naming of a new genus.
Its name means “lake hunter from La Rioja”, referring to both its locality in Argentina and its likely paleoenvironment. It is also one of the youngest known baryonychine spinosaurids in the fossil record.
items.freeTags: South America, Late Cretaceous, Riojavenatrix lacustris
items.location: Fossil from La Rioja, Spain (CMS tag says S. America but fossil is European)

items.name: Araripesuchus manzanensis
items.description:
A newly described species from the Cretaceous period, part of the Uruguaysuchidae family, named after the site "El Manzano" in La Buitrera, Argentina.
Unlike modern crocodiles, this group had relatively long limbs, suggesting they moved in a very different way—likely capable of running or galloping.
This artwork was created to celebrate its discovery.
items.freeTags: South America, Late Cretaceous, Araripesuchus manzanensis

items.name: Oviraptor protecting its nest
items.description:
This animation, offers a glimpse into a hypothetical behavior of Oviraptor—often depicted as a nest raider due to its name (Latin: egg thief).
However, fossils tell a different story: the first specimen was found atop a nest, likely protecting it, not stealing from it. Modern research shows Oviraptor was likely a caring parent.
A great example of how scientific interpretations evolve over time.

items.name: Kostensuchus atrox
items.description:
After a long wait, the new crocodyliform discovered in the Chorrillo Formation, about 30 km southeast of the city of El Calafate, has finally been published.
Kostensuchus atrox is a new taxon that joins the family of Peirosaurids, a group of notosuchian crocodyliforms. It is a distant relative of the “Boar Crocodile” (Kaprosuchus).
The material corresponds mainly to the animal’s anterior region, with a very well-preserved and articulated skull, along with cervical and dorsal vertebrae, its pectoral and pelvic girdles, and both humeri.
"I want to thank @poldiego and @fernando.novas.5 for trusting me with this work and for all the valuable feedback that led to the result you see in the animation.
Congratulations to the whole team, and welcome Kostensuchus atrox!"

items.name: Futalognkosaurus dukei
items.description:
The African elephant is the largest terrestrial vertebrate that currently exists, and although other mammals have grown larger than others, the sauropods are much larger than any terrestrial animal in the history of life.
In the hemisphere, titanosaurs predominated, and we found very famous taxones like Argentinosaurus huinculensis or Patagotitan majorum.
And although the record of gigantic animals is fragmentary and rare, a large portion of animal species has been preserved, Futalognkosaurus poses all over its cervical vertebras (vertebras of the neck) and dorsal vertebras up to the frame, together with its sacral vertebras.

As today, success is not guaranteed for predators who take advantage of every opportunity to get food.
